task:
FIX SIX REVIEW FINDINGS ON PR #799 (v3-system-search-validate-constraints action). Target branch codex/run-38012804725-1, expected head 3054dcc; fail closed and write nothing if it moved. Only scripts/operator/actions/v3-system-search-validate-constraints.sh and tests/test_v3_system_search_validate_constraints.py may change (CHANGES.md only if wording there becomes wrong).

F1 (P2, ~line 212, PID file path): `docker exec -d ... sh -c 'cd DIR && (psql ...) & echo $! > run.pid'` — shell precedence backgrounds the whole `cd && (...)` list, so `echo $! > run.pid` runs in the container's original cwd and run.pid never lands in /tmp/edfinder-validate-constraints. FIX: use absolute paths everywhere and group correctly, e.g. `sh -c 'cd /tmp/edfinder-validate-constraints && { (psql ... -f /tmp/edfinder-validate-constraints/run.sql > /tmp/edfinder-validate-constraints/run.log 2>&1; echo "exit=$?" >> /tmp/edfinder-validate-constraints/run.log) & echo $! > /tmp/edfinder-validate-constraints/run.pid; }'`. Add a test asserting the launch command writes the pid to the absolute path.

F2 (P2, ~line 304, status exit code): status prints a receipt with status 'stopped' when a query fails but the process exits 0, so the workflow goes green. FIX: status_operation exits 1 whenever failures is non-empty (after printing the receipt). Test: with the ledger query failing, exit code is 1 and the receipt still prints.

F3 (P2, ~line 52, Python runtime): the receipts call bare `python3`, which may be an older interpreter. FIX: select the interpreter like v3-derived-lifecycle-status.sh does — prefer `python3.14`, else `python3` only if it proves CPython 3.14 via `-c 'import platform, sys; raise SystemExit(0 if platform.python_implementation()=="CPython" and sys.version_info[:2]==(3,14) else 1)'`; otherwise print a stopped receipt (plain printf JSON, failure python314_required) and exit 1. Use the selected $PYTHON_BIN for every receipt. Tests: stub PATH must provide python3.14 (a wrapper to sys.executable) — assert the script uses it (e.g. the stub logs its invocation) and that with no python3.14 and a python3 that reports 3.13 the script stops with python314_required.

F4 (P2, ~line 72, db_writes_performed): VALIDATE CONSTRAINT writes pg_constraint.convalidated, so the start receipt's `db_writes_performed: false` is wrong when a validation was launched. FIX: rename the semantics: in the start receipt set `db_writes_performed` to true when catalog_validation_launched is true (and false otherwise), keep `data_rows_modified: false`, and add `catalog_writes: "pg_constraint.convalidated only"`. Update tests accordingly (nothing_to_validate and stopped paths keep db_writes_performed false).

F5 (P2, ~line 297, status hash mismatch): when the ledger has a different 010 hash, status still reports success/all_validated. FIX: if the ledger hash is present but != MIGRATION_SHA add failure 'migration_010_hash_mismatch'; if absent add 'migration_010_not_applied'; both make status 'stopped' (and exit 1 per F2). all_validated may still be computed but the receipt must not be 'success'. Test both.

F6 (P2, ~line 138, idle sessions): pg_stat_activity.query holds the LAST query for idle sessions, so a finished VALIDATE in an idle persistent session blocks every later start. FIX: in active_validation() add `AND state <> 'idle'` (keep 'active' and 'idle in transaction' variants). Test: the SQL contains `state <> 'idle'`.

Keep all 18 constraint names, the lock/statement timeouts, the detached design and the forbidden-string guarantees. Update the header comment where behaviour changed (db_writes_performed semantics, python selection).

VALIDATION (paste commands and counts): 1. bash -n the script  2. python -m pytest tests/test_v3_system_search_validate_constraints.py tests/test_v3_derived_lifecycle_status.py -q -p no:cacheprovider  3. shellcheck if available  4. git diff --name-only 3054dcc lists only the allowed files. Commit message: 'ops: validate-constraints action — absolute pid path, fail-closed status, CPython 3.14 receipts, honest catalog-write flag, idle-session filter'.
